placements.why: The document introduces a deployment gate decision with defined scope and ownership — an organizational-strategy category for release management that nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers. The content names a category of governance policy, not merely a single fact.
placements.title: Release and deployment governance as a first-class organizational concern
placements.theme: Release management establishes gating policies and ownership for deployment pipelines to prevent unverified artifacts from reaching production environments.

placements.title: Signed release manifests become a hard gate for Meridian deployments
placements.theme: Meridian deployments require a signed release manifest before shipping to staging or production, established after two unsigned artifacts reached staging last quarter.
placements.why: src-1 declares the gate policy (signed manifest required before any Meridian deployment ships). src-2 supplies the motivating incident — two unsigned artifacts reaching staging — as evidence for why the gate exists. src-4 restates the gate, src-5 defines its scope (staging and production), and src-6 names its owner (Quinton Fairweather). Together they support one thematic leaf: the signed-manifest deployment gate as a reusable subject future envelopes may extend or revise. No existing leaf fits, so this is a mint.
